entries.lesson_title: Complex Exponentials as LTI System Inputs
entries.core_move: Interpret a complex exponential $e^{j\omega t}$ as a single-frequency probe input for an LTI system, identifying $\omega$ as the frequency whose response determines output scaling and phase.

entries.lesson_title: Deriving the Output for a Complex Exponential Input
entries.core_move: Derive the LTI output for $x(t)=e^{j\omega t}$ by substituting the input into the convolution integral and factoring out $e^{j\omega t}$ to identify the remaining integral as the system's complex gain at $\omega$.
Interpret $H(j\omega)$ as the frequency-indexed complex gain that an LTI system applies to a complex exponential input $e^{j\omega t}$, producing a same-frequency output.

entries.lesson_title: Frequency Response as Fourier Transform of $h(t)$
entries.core_move: Compute $H(j\omega)$ as the Fourier transform of the impulse response $h(t)$ and interpret it as the complex gain applied to sinusoidal components at angular frequency $\omega$.

entries.lesson_title: Sinusoids as Eigenfunctions of LTI Systems
entries.core_move: Use the frequency-response relation $H(j\omega)$ to show that sinusoidal inputs are eigenfunctions of LTI systems, changing only amplitude and phase while keeping frequency unchanged.
Recognize that a sinusoidal input to a continuous-time LTI system produces an output sinusoid at the same angular frequency, with frequency response affecting only amplitude and phase.
Compute the output sinusoid's amplitude by multiplying the input amplitude by $|H(j\omega)|$ at the input frequency for sinusoidal steady-state passage through an LTI system.
Compute the output sinusoid's phase by evaluating $\angle H(j\omega)$ at the input frequency and adding that shift to the input phase while leaving the frequency unchanged.
